data.result:
"# C# style

The `.editorconfig` enforces the mechanical part at build time. This file names the rules
it cannot express.

## Layout

- File-scoped namespaces. `using` directives outside the namespace, `System.*` first.
- Allman braces. Braces on every `if`, `else`, loop and `using`, even for one statement.
- Block bodies for methods and constructors; expression bodies for properties and accessors.
  A setter with more than one statement gets a block over several lines.
- No `#region`. One blank line between members, never two.
- Blank lines inside a method:
  - A block (`if`, loop, `using`, `try`) gets a blank line before and after it, also when it
    is a guard clause or holds one statement. The same for a multi-line initializer.
  - A comment inside a method starts a unit: blank line before it, none after it.
  - `InitializeComponent()` at the start and the call that finishes the work at the end, such
    as `RecalculateTotals()`, stand alone, also after a single statement.
  - Single-line statements that form one unit stay together: two sample rows, three resets.
  - No blank line directly after `{` or before `}`.
- A statement stays on one line up to 160 characters; argument lists are not wrapped for
  length alone. Longer statements break at a seam: before a chained `.Call()`, `??`, `?`, `:`,
  `&&`, `||`, the operator starts the next line; or after a comma, the remaining arguments on
  one continuation line. Exceptions: a configuration chain such as `AddMcpServer().With…()`
  keeps one call per line; parameters with a `[Description]` stay one per line;
  `[Description]` strings never wrap.
- Member order: constants → static fields → instance fields → events → properties →
  constructor → public methods → event handlers → private methods.
- File ends with the closing brace and one newline, no blank line after it.

## Language

- `var` everywhere. Explicit accessibility modifier on every member. No `this.`.
- Language keywords (`string`, `int`), not framework types (`String`, `Int32`).
- Pattern matching over `is`/`as` plus cast. Inline `out var`.
- `if (expr is { } value)` when the value is only used inside the block.
- Combine related null and type checks into one `if` instead of several early returns.
- Guard clauses belong in the called method, not at the call site.
- `sealed` where inheritance is not intended. `readonly` fields where possible.
- `async`/`await`, never `.Result` or `.Wait()`. Async methods end in `Async`.
- Catch the specific exception type and handle it or rethrow. Never swallow.
- Named constants instead of magic numbers; the name says what the value is.

## Naming

- PascalCase for types, members, constants and local functions.
- `_camelCase` for all private fields, static ones too. No `s_`.
- camelCase for locals and parameters.
- Full words, no abbreviations: `deviceContext`, not `dc`; `quantity`, not `q`.
- P/Invoke methods keep PascalCase; the native name goes into `EntryPoint`.
- WPF event handlers keep the `Control_Event` pattern that XAML generates.
"

"# Comments and prose

Applies to code comments, `[Description]` texts, README, cards and commit messages.

## Language

- Plain, simple English. Short sentences, active voice, no jargon, no marketing words.
- Swaps: "in order to" → "to", "leverage" / "utilise" → "use", "constitutes a" → "is a".
- No dash as a thought dash, neither `-` nor `–` nor `—`. Use a period, comma, colon or semicolon.
- No filler sentences. A comment that repeats the code is deleted.

## What gets a comment

- The reason, not the mechanics: a deliberate gap, a workaround, an OS or library constraint,
  an order of operations that matters, a limit and why it has that value.
- No XML docs, no `<summary>`. A class gets a `//` block directly above its declaration that
  says what it is for and how it is used.
- MCP tools: the `[Description]` is what the agent reads. Name what the tool does, the fallback
  order and the unit of every parameter.
- `// NOTE:` marks something that looks wrong but is intended, such as a gap a card will close.
  A NOTE about the whole class sits directly above the class, not at the top of the file.

## Shape

- A comment sits above the code it explains, never at the end of the line, except for a
  single named value such as `// 2 = PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT`.
- Multi-line comments: the first line is the longest, about 80 characters, up to 100 when
  that avoids a short last line. Following lines break within that width. A line never ends
  with a conjunction such as "and" or "or".
- Commit messages: first line says what changed, the body says why and how it was verified.
"

data.result:
"# General rules

- Keep changes minimal and focused on the request. No drive-by refactors, renames or reformatting.
- Prefer explicit, readable code over clever code.
- Before adding a helper, check whether one exists. Remove dead code that a change leaves behind.
- Do not add NuGet packages unless the task needs them.
- Never modify `bin/**`, `obj/**` or generated files (`*.g.cs`).
- Never speculate. Verify a claim about an API or a behavior against the code or the assembly before
  recommending or applying it. If that is not possible, say so and mark the recommendation as unverified.
- Every interactive control in `src/InvoiceApp` has an `AutomationId`. The MCP tools address controls by it.
- The code is read by people who follow the article, not only by the compiler. Write for them.
"

card: The total ignores the discount

RecalculateTotals now parses the discount percent and multiplies the subtotal by (1 - percent / 100). An empty or non-numeric discount parses to 0, and the subtotal stays undiscounted.
Verified live: with items worth 100,00 and a discount of 10 the total showed 90,00, "abc" and an empty field gave 100,00, and the subtotal stayed 100,00.

data.text:
The discount now reduces the total. I committed it as 210e9d8.

I checked each acceptance criterion in the running app. The app uses German number formatting, so the values below show a comma.

- **Before the fix:** with the two sample items (subtotal 88,80) and a discount of 10, the total stayed at 88,80.
- **100.00 with a 10 discount:** I added an item to bring the subtotal to 100,00. With a discount of 10, the total showed 90,00.
- **Empty or non-numeric discount:** typing "abc" gave a total of 100,00. Clearing the field also gave 100,00. Neither produced an error.
- **Subtotal:** it stayed at 100,00 throughout.

The change is in `RecalculateTotals` in `MainWindow.xaml.cs`. It reads the discount percent and multiplies the subtotal by `1 - percent / 100`. A text that can't be parsed counts as 0.

I didn't add any limits on the discount, so a negative value raises the total and a value over 100 makes it negative. The card doesn't ask for limits.
